| [TERM-125](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-125.md) v11 | independent execution gate | The assistant's, offered at step 12 of the filing of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" and accepted by the owner on 2026-11-16, renamed at the review of 2026-11-16. A gate is a step the executor cannot pass on its own. Two neighbouring properties are kept apart from it: execution impedance (does the step add time or cost?) and intervention opportunity (can another party bring an objection that changes the process?). A standing limit enforced by another's mechanism is a gate without impedance and need not be an opportunity; a rubber-stamp approval is a gate with impedance and no real opportunity; a channel for challenging a process's rules can be an opportunity without gating ordinary execution. Whether a gate is procedural friction, in the sense of the owner's claim ([CLAIM-710](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-710.md)), is left open. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
